text: Welcome to Tabletop Combat Simulator
Tabletop Combat Simulator (TCS) aims to mimic the way Warhammer is played on the tabletop. Players will take turns activating their units, as they progress through different phases.
This tour will provides an introduction to controls and features of TCS.
Start
Phase Controls
In the top right of your screen you can find the controls that allow you to progress to the next phase as well as give you information about the current active player.

You can progress to the next phase by either clicking the 'fast forward' button, or the square button that follows the current active phase. You can recognize active phases by their distinct golden border.

Phases progress as follows; a battleshock phase in which units rout when losing combat -> a Hero Phase in which you are supposed to cast any damaging spells or summons -> a Movement phase that allows units to move about for a set duration -> a Shooting phase in which ranged units can fire their missile weapons -> a Charge phase that allows units to bridge the gap between them and an opponent -> a Fight phase in which both players get to activate their units to fight anohter unit within engagement range
Unit Activations

Units have abilities that allow them to perform 'Activations' depending on the current active phase. Such activations allow a unit to move and or fight depending on whether they are engaged with an enemy or other relevant factors.

Moving & Running allows units to move about, but beware that you cannot run into combat; a unit will be forcefully stopped at the engagement range of an opponent. Charging is a targetted ability that does allow the unit to move within engagement range, but has a chance to fail. The further the charge the greater the chance of failure.

Units can Shoot and Fight in their respective phases, it's up to the player's discretion how and when abilities are used. Note that to get out of combat with another unit you have to use a retreat command that prevents your unit from taking other actions that turn.
Unit Info

In the Unit Info panel you can see when a Unit is activated and for how long. A text bar on top provides you with information about internal rolls that have been made and the passive effect bar shows when a unit has their attacks or movement disabled.

The Unit Status bar atop the Info Panel shows you, after activating a unit, some info about that activation. Typically the duration of the activation is shown, but sometimes you can find information about the failure to activate an ability, like failing a dice roll.

There are 3 main passives that govern your units, Inactive Fight, Shoot and Stationary. Note that they disappear for the duration of their respective activations to allow a unit to either melee, fire missiles, or move about.

Phases
Tabletop Combat Simulator is fought over multiple phases each round. Units have different abilities throughout each phase to exercise different tasks.
Below you will find information on each phase:
Hero Phase

The Hero Phase starts off with a morale check for each unit in the active player's army. When their leadership dips below a configured threshold, the unit must make a Break Check. A dice is cast and if the result exceeds the current leadership of the unit they will withdraw from combat.

Following the Morale Check of a players army they are awarded Winds of Magic for each caster-type unit they field in their armies. The amount of Winds per wizard can be configured through the [[sl:battle_tcs_config]]settings menu[[/sl]].

Afterwards the player may assume control over their units and issue orders to activate abilities or cast spells. Buffs and Debuffs that do not have a healing or damaging component will remain active until the player's next Hero Phase. Note that many spells have a higher chance of miscasting than they would typically in regular TW.

Some spells require the caster to fire a projectile. Due to the inner workings of the mod, such spells can only be cast during the Shoot Phase and only while under the effect of a [[sl:battle_tcs_activations]]Shoot Activation[[/sl]].
Move Phase

The Hero Phase is followed by the Move Phase. During this phase you may move your units about on the battlefield through various [[sl:battle_tcs_activations]]Activations[[/sl]]. Each unit is alotted a certain Movement Budget. This represents the distance a unit can move about, or use to wheel their formation around. Using the Unit Status Panel you can see how much movement budget is left for the selected unit, and how much movement a Move Activation would cost under your cursor.

Moving into combat range of an enemy unit is prohibited and will also result in a failed movement, but fear not, you may still Activate your unit at no penalty to your movement budget. Should a unit move into the [[sl:battle_tcs_controls]]Engagement Range[[/sl]] of a unit during an activation however, they will stop moving immediately and be locked in place. Any further movement will immediately result in them halting to prevent them from getting any closer to that enemy.

You can [[sl:battle_tcs_config]]configure[[/sl]] a buffer zone around units in which you receive a warning and a chance to issue a new Move Activation after a unit enters this zone during a move. You only receive one warning per unit per round however.

A regular Move Activation requires you to click on the battlefield to determine the destination of the move. If the destination is outside of reach, it will be reflected in the [[sl:battle_tcs_controls]]Status Pane[[/sl]]l and you can Activate your Unit again. Moving into combat range of an enemy unit is prohibited and will also result in a failed movement, but fear not, you may still Activate your unit at no penalty to your movement budget.

When engaged in combat, the only Movement Activation that is permitted is a Retreat Activation. This will withdraw your unit from combat and send them towards a nearby battlefield edge. The unit will stop retreating once outside of [[sl:battle_tcs_controls]]Engagement Range[[/sl]] of any enemy unit.

On the flanks, you might sometimes wish to Wheel a unit about to face an oncoming charge. Using the Wheel Activation you can select a direction and have the unit stay roughly in place, but reform to face the direction of your cursor.
Tabletop Combat Simulator

Tabletop Combat Simulator is a gameplay mod for Total War: WARHAMMER III that aims to recreate the feel of tabletop skirmishes inside the real-time battles: tighter unit control, simplified morale interactions, scaled damage, and modular rules for custom scenarios.

t slows down the battles considerably, to the effect of allowing players to zoom in on their units and admire the combat from up close, without the pressure of micromanaging units into the ideal position or relying on reaction time to counter a flanking manouver.

This mod intends to be served as a framework and does not aim to deliver a balanced play experience. To that end a balance mod, with perhaps a compatibility submod, is required to be installed alongside of it.

Lastly you may opt to Run Activate a unit. This will simply roll a dice internally and add an amount of movement to the unit's budget accordingly. The maximum extra distance can be configured in the [[sl:battle_tcs_config]]settings menu[[/sl]].
Shoot Phase
After moving your units in position, it is time for the Shoot Phase. In this phase your units can use their Shoot Activation to unlock their ranged attacks and rain destruction on their enemies.
Remember that some spells and abilities require this Activation to be performed.
Charge Phase

To bridge the gap left by the engagement range of units, you will have to issue a Charge Activation to your units. This lets them target an enemy and cross any zone of influence of enemy units. Internally, before a charge, a dice is rolled and the result is checked to the distance of the charge. Should the roll not be enough to make the charge, your unit will be rooted in place until their next available movement phase.
Beware of relying on long charges! Your units may turn into sitting ducks during your opponent's turn should they fail to charge into combat. You only have once chance at every charge.
The distance nad charge rolls can be configured in the [[sl:battle_tcs_config]]settings menu[[/sl]] in case you would like to tweak the numbers.
Combat Phase

Finally it is time to spill some blood in Khorne's name. Every unit within engagement range of an enemy, both from the active player and the opponent's, can use their Fight Activation to unlock their deadly potential. For a short duration the unit is allowed to move to get closer to their targets, or perhaps to envelop them. And until their timer runs out they can deal damage to their targets or whoever comes in between.
Fighting requires you to choose a target, but units will attack anything in melee range once they stop moving. It does however allow you to focus most of your attacks at one unit.
It is up to you and your opponent whether you activate in turns during the Combat Phase, or if you go for an all out brawl and Activate your fighters in rapid succession.
Fighting is done by duration, so if you would like a more deadly game, you can increase the fighting time int the [[sl:battle_tcs_config]]settings menu[[/sl]].
